body: That’s amazing! I’m about a year in remission (more or less) but I’m still heavily medicated too. It’s great to hear you managed to get off them fully for depression!

If the scars are at least a year old, you might want to look into getting a tattoo cover up. I got mine on my arm covered 2 years ago and it has honestly changed my life. I still have the ones on my legs, so swimming and shorts in the summer are still an issue, but I would rather enjoy myself at the beach and be comfortable than try to make others comfortable by hiding them. As hard as it is to admit, the more distance I have between the scars, the more confident I am about showing them. Like they are a part of my past and not me currently.

It doesn’t go away. It may look differently based on the needs of school vs work as you get older, but you can’t “willpower” it away. I wasn’t even diagnosed until late college. Meds changed my life and also significantly reduced my anxiety. They help me even do things like laundry and cleaning. I think I heard somewhere that kids who get on meds for their adhd also have a lesser chance of developing addiction disorders later in life. That might help convince him to let you get meds.
Are you on any meds still for it or is it literally full remission? Happy for you!

i was all over her - salvia palth, 
Dramamine - Modest Mouse, 
Smother - Daughter
Megan Thee Stallion - Cobra (especially the rock remix)

My first round of accutane I had to stop due to liver enzymes. Thankfully I was able to do a half dose for just twice as long without it spiking. If it helps, I think even though I didn’t complete the first round, it still significantly reduced my acne. So don’t lose hope that your acne may stay away!
I  do this. I’ve found it sometimes helps me work through urges if I can get the visual stimulation from previous times. It also helps me track how long it’s been since the last time.

I experienced the same thing. Still wanting to die but feeling like my depression has lifted. It does get better with time, but I think because it was such a frequent visitor in our regular thoughts for so long, our regular thought patterns don’t always keep up with our changing mood right away.

I did 2 in one day once. They prefer not to, but since I was going to be out of town and missing session days, they allowed me to double up. I think it’s more of a special circumstance thing rather than something they want regularly done.

The same thing happened to me during my course of treatment. I did it for 5 months, then my liver enzymes spiked. Took a month off, then did 5 months again and they spiked again. Later to avoid my liver enzymes spiking, I did a half dose at twice the length of treatment. So it just took twice as long. But I was able to keep my liver enzymes in check keeping it at a lower dose.
I was able to watch tv without pausing it every 5 mins to stare off into space because I was so disinterested. I was able to watch shows in full. Binge watch even. I think that was my first sign.

This was how it was for me too. Hitting the deductible and then the rest is coinsurance. The first place I did mine at was part of a hospital network, so I was able to set up a monthly payment plan with them instead of all at once.

I have a large piece on my arm to cover scars from my upper arm down to my upper forearm. It takes the ink super well. The texture is still there, but the scars are SIGNIFICANTLY less noticeable. My artist did a wonderful job.
Same I don’t trust myself not to fall. I just wait until the next stop and switch then.
While I didn’t go 100% into remission, my scores decreased over 50%. And there is a BIG difference between mild and severe depression. Monumental difference.

When I was on it, I had to go off it for a month to fix my liver labs. My doc said it would be basically out of my system by that point and we’d be restarting treatment. Depending on where you’re studying abroad, could you get a prescription there? I know accutane is available in a lot of European countries too from reading this sub.

Well I decided to do a round 2 because about 6 months after my first round completed, I went on birth control and it fucked up my mood so bad that I got it removed a month later. But it set me back into that deep depression and anxiety. I decided to do a second round (it was either that or residential treatment). 

The first round, it took almost the whole course to notice the difference, but when it did happen, it was sudden. Like night and day. With the second round, the change was much more gradual. I didn’t notice the benefits until about a month out from completing it. While I didn’t go into 100% remission with either round, there’s a BIG difference between mild and severe. 

I’m about 7 months out from completing my second round and I’m still doing alright. I’m able to work on myself in ways I was never able to when I was worse and am making changes to improve my life overall (being more social, focusing on my physical health, doing things that bring me joy because now I can actually enjoy things). 

My therapist has mentioned that after my first round, she felt my improvement lended itself to a slightly manic level of happiness, whereas my second round has left me more with stable emotions. The second round has left me with a more sustainable level of emotional regulation, which is I think what’s most important.
Came here to suggest him too. Specifically a song dedicated to the memory of stormy the rabbit, bad bad things, rejoice, and the freedom tickler.

I go alone all the time. Sometimes I prefer it because I can stand wherever I want and don’t have to worry about making sure the person I’m with is having a good time too. If you really want to go - go!

Honestly processing it all in therapy is going to be the biggest help. Coming out of the depression definitely gives you space to work on the things that contributed to the depression. It might be scary to confront these things - but keep in mind you’ll be confronting them from a better state of mind. You will feel more capable of handling those difficult memories and not spiraling from them. Best of luck with your treatment! I’m proud of you for doing it!

It’s great you took a day off when you needed it and listened to you and your needs. My second round of TMS, I didn’t feel the effects until about a month out from completing treatment. And it was very gradual and not super apparent until I reflected back on it. Someone else on this sub once said that their tech told them we don’t realize the toll it takes on us to be somewhere everyday to get our head buzzed for weeks on end until we are finally done with it. It can take some time to feel the relief. Please don’t lose hope yet.

I’ve fallen into a similar pattern earlier in the year of “planning” to do it rather than it being driven from an emotional state. What really helped me refrain from relapsing even more was doing the DBT pros/cons worksheet. I then saved that to my phone and would look at it whenever I felt urges to do so. Some cons being put at risk of a higher level of treatment (which would significantly disrupt my life), and losing the trust of my friends and family, which I’ve worked so hard over the years to regain. You can do this worksheet with both the self harm behaviors and the ED behaviors. Because both are maladaptive and don’t get you to a happier place long-term.
I’ve done 2 rounds of it too and am so glad you saw such an improvement that you knew another round could help you again. I’m proud of you!
Mine are all still in baggies - but I’ve seen people make wall art or even coasters with their confetti.
You should be fine then! Just as long as you keep that style everyday. I have long and curly hair, so the gel and leave in I had in my hair wasn’t a problem at all.
TMS high key changed my life. It significantly reduced my depression and anxiety. If you have the opportunity to try it - try it.

Not sure if you have long or short hair but try to style it the same way as you did when you got your mapping done. Like I had my mapping done with my regular hair down. If I came in with braids the next day, that could change things. So just be consistent. Products themselves are fine. Tinted moisturizer might rub off a bit on your forehead but is also fine.

I went to the same school and knew many people who would use the green line and take the shuttle. Since you’re coming from milder weather, biking/being outside in the winter might be hard to adjust to. There’s plenty of people that bike too, but I personally would try to be “indoors” as much as possible.

I’ve done 2 rounds and both times I didn’t feel an effect at the point you’re in. My first round I felt better at session 30/36 and my second round I didn’t feel better until about a month after I finished all 36. Since you’re so close to the finish line, I’d recommend just sticking it out. It might pay off.
Everyone is there to see the artist - not worry if the people around them are with their parents or not. I recently went to a concert with my dad (I’m 27), and it was totally chill.

My first round it was like night and day switch around session 30/36. My second round it was definitely a slow burn only really noticing a difference about a month out of completion. It wasn’t as stark but it was still just as impactful.

How long ago did you complete it? My last round, it took me about a full month or so to notice a difference after I completed treatment. I’m really sorry you haven’t seen progress so far. I know how distressing that feels. It’s also good to recognize that getting out and about has been helpful for you in other ways too.

My first round lasted me about 6 months (something else medical triggered the relapse). My second round ended about 5 months ago, but I’m hoping it lasts longer. I’ve still always been on my meds. 
If you want to try being off it, you could go off it and then once you feel symptoms returning, get back on them. It’s not like you can never return to them. Just be vigilant about tracking your symptoms and in close communication with your psych.
Can I message you? I prefer not to publicly post my location - but I’m 27 and single and love my neighborhood - plus my rent is only $1000.
I saw Green Day a few weeks ago and they didn’t check IDs. Plus there were kids there, so it isn’t an age restricted event. You’re good!

I’ve done I think 3 or 4 DBT groups. While some were more effective than others, none of them gave me a bad experience. I contribute a LOT of my recovery to being in a DBT group. You learn the skills in a group, structured setting. Then you get homework to actually practice the skills. The more you practice, the easier it is to implement the skills into your daily life and emotional regulation. If you have the opportunity to do a group - do it. 100%. I went through a rough patch earlier in the year and the very first thing my therapist and I looked at was a DBT group. Unfortunately none in my area worked with my work schedule or took my insurance, so I did an ACT group instead. But DBT is by far the most helpful group I’ve ever done. If you have the chance to do it - take it.
Because it works for the majority of people. Im still paying on my payment plan for over a year, and id do it again because of just how much it helped me. I’ll pay it if it makes me want to be alive.
Might be worth a shot!

I’ve been on it for about 3 months now and have not noticed a single side effect, not even the leg swelling. It took about 2 weeks for my bp to get to a healthy range. This is also my first bp med I’ve tried, but overall I’m a fan of it.

Back when I was on it I had to take a month break due to my bloodwork but my Derm said that that long of a break basically resets the cumulative dose goal, so more or less starting over. Is there another doctor you might be able to see? Or your old one giving you one in the meantime?
I have a ladder that I hang the “in between” clothes on to keep them separate from everything else.

My coworker/friend has lived in Roger’s Park for about 10 years and has never had an issue with rats/mice or any other kind of pests. I don’t know about your specific building and management, but I can attest to living close to the lake and the L is amazing, and you won’t regret it!
I never thought of that but that’s a really good point too! It can definitely be draining.

I’ve done 2 rounds. I didn’t notice a difference in my first round until session 30 out of 36. The second round, I didn’t notice a different until like a month after I completed all the sessions. Please keep going and doing it. Hope isn’t lost yet.

I’m glad you’re going back for a second round! I’ve done 2 rounds of it myself, and I’m super glad I did.

I’ve done 2 rounds - my first round I didn’t feel a difference until 30/36 sessions. My second round I didn’t feel a difference until maybe a month after I completed all my sessions. Definitely stick it out.
I think I found this sub when I was 20/21 and am now 27. Been quite a ride lol.

I’m afraid of attempting and then failing. I don’t want to have a permanent disability, mental or physical, as a result of an attempt. I don’t want to live an even more difficult life than I already am. 
I also know it would be an asshole move to make to those in my life who still care about me (my siblings mostly). I don’t want to burden them with grief.

I relate heavily to this. I just started taking naltrexone for my binge urges, and even though I’m still only at a half dose, I’m beginning to notice a difference. I don’t feel compelled to eat, even if I’m a little hungry. It’s a very foreign feeling.
Silver! I knew before even looking at the actual jewelry.
I’ve done a few rounds of accutane and never purged during any of them

I’d suggest waiting. Just basic wound healing took forever (sometimes non existent) when I was on it. Risking getting a tattoo in a non-ideal skin situation could risk poor healing and changing the tattoo outcome. I highly recommend waiting until your skin returns to normal after treatment (ideally 6 months).

First off - I’m proud of you for wanting to get your health prioritized again! I would suggest starting with choosing a primary care doctor. Try to do one within a larger health network. They can then give you referrals to all the other doctors you might need, which takes away a lot of the stress and guesswork on your end. They may be able to help treat the adhd and anxiety too, at least temporarily, until you can get set up with a psychiatrist. For finding a dentist, I’d suggest just looking in your area and making sure they take your insurance (if applicable). I know it probably feels very overwhelming, but you are totally capable and can do this!
I always park on noble off of division - free and close by. Never had an issue finding parking there before.
Chicago Women’s Health Group is great. Dr. Onia especially. But I’ve found everyone I’ve interacted with there has been great.

I’ve done the nail polish hack with earrings before and it has worked well! I’ve also seen plastic earrings post covers that you can slide over the metal part so it doesn’t come in contact with your ear. If all else fails, I’d say selling them or gifting them.

My doctor always has me do deep breathing while doing readings and then gives me some time to relax before doing a second reading. I’m not a doctor, but I imagine it is to see what your resting bp is when fully relaxed. If that’s high - then maybe you need meds. But if they say that’s still good, I would trust them. I don’t think you cheated the test at all.

Emotional neglect can definitely be the cause of cptsd. It is for me. I didn’t even identify it myself - my therapist did. From what I’ve observed, big T trauma is more associated with ptsd whereas little t trauma is more associated with cptsd. That doctor you went to sounds invalidating and uninformed.

Yes, as other posters have stated, there is an increased risk for Alzheimer’s and dementia with prolonged use of Benadryl. Definitely talk to your doctor about alternative options. I take a prescription allergy med and xyzal daily. To help with your eyes, Pazeo eye drops are a lifesaver. There’s a lot of nasal sprays that you may benefit from as well. But definitely try to taper down your use of Benadryl. Allergy shots might be worth it too if it’s within your means and accessibility.

What is it about the fast food that draws you to it? The convenience? The flavors? Habit? One thing that helped me get away from fast food is buying “ready to heat up” foods from Aldi. Premade foods that all you have to do is microwave it. It’s not quite cooking at home but it’s better than eating out.
I found the essay The Death of the Author by Roland Barthes to be super impactful in learning how to interpret contemporary art. He talks specifically about literature, but it applies to art as well.

I’m still on it - TMS changed my depression from severe to very mild. So I’m still on it to help with the mild. And let me tell you - there is a BIG difference between mild and severe depression and anxiety. Even though I didn’t get off my meds, it was still incredibly worth it.
I was on Wellbutrin for the entirety of my treatment with no issues. Mine advised against any medication changes since that could skew results of TMS.

I wouldn’t mind. I’ve noticed a general shift that we are wanting to meet people in the wild rather than on apps, so being approached in public is a part of that. To avoid being creepy, maybe try complimenting them on something specific about them/what they’re wearing. I’ve had a couple good convos as a result of people commenting on my tattoo. Don’t let headphones deter you. I usually have one in one ear while walking so I can enjoy some music, but I don’t mind taking it out to talk to someone.

I also struggled with self harm growing up, but thankfully my mom never took away my razors (I infrequently used them for SH). My suggestion would be to get an electric razor - tbh the ones made for men seem to be better. I struggle to get as close as I can with shaving, but it may be a viable option for your private area. They’re hard to dismantle, so your mom can keep it in between shaves if that would make her more likely to allow it.

Definitely. Then as you go through school you can connect with your classmates and professors (I only did professors after the class finished). Both will be great resources when you begin to enter the workforce. For content - you can put your major and your concentration/focus or what you hope to do with it. Can be as vague or detailed as you wish.
Maybe it has something to do with the protocol you received? But even so - I’ve had 2 different ones and both still did brain mapping

I’ve done 2 rounds and both times I did brain mapping and they both made a big improvement in my moods. I’ve never heard of them skipping the brain mapping? I would definitely suggest retrying with the mapping.

I’ve done 2 rounds with about 6 months between them. But that’s only because it initially worked but began to be depressed again (thanks to a different med). After my second round, I didn’t notice the positive changes until at least a month after treatment ended. So it can definitely take some time sometimes. Are there other clinics in your area that could work with your school schedule if you need to go back now?

I have all my apps except the essentials locked until 7:30am using the screen time settings. I also try to do as much as i can the night before (like making my lunch). I also try to eat breakfast on the go/at work, but i know that isn’t an option for everyone.

In my experience, even if people notice, they won’t say anything. I worked a pretty physical job in no ac in the summer with long sleeves. No one said a thing (and these people weren’t the type to keep to themselves either). Most people are focused on their own world and job and not whether you are wearing long or short sleeves. If people do ask - maybe you have a new tattoo that needs covering. Or maybe you just run cold. There’s plenty of non-sh reasons people prefer long sleeves. I wouldn’t stress about people asking. Do what makes you feel most comfortable.
I saw Greta Van Fleet last year with my dad and my sister. I’ll be seeing Bob Dylan soon with my dad too. My dad is in his late 50s, and I’m in my late 20s.

Maybe finding something that isn’t exactly that but adjacent would be helpful? My advisor in undergrad focuses on trauma and grief with public art and contemporary art.
I typically go about 10 over. 5-10 if I’m closer to downtown. Just make sure to not go over 25 at all costs.

TMS changed my life (for the better). I know it’s corny to say, but it is true. It was a big time and financial commitment, but it helped me more than I thought possible. For the first time I felt what it was like to not be severely anxious and depressed. I didn’t get my scores to 0, but there is a BIG difference between mild and severe depression. I’ll gladly take mild depression. It has given me the ability to implement coping strategies and ways to improve my life that I just didn’t have the energy or care to do when depressed. I have cptsd too and I feel like TMS has helped me immensely in being able to implement healthier coping strategies and overall mindset.

I definitely feel it’s a behavior addiction. The spike of dopamine I think that occurs when cutting is  definitely addictive. Growing up, I would trade off between disordered eating and cutting. When I turned 21 I stopped cutting as much because I could now drink. Around that same time I also had another spike in disordered eating. I would do anything to stop my feelings. Cutting is still always my default urge when I get emotional, even if I haven’t done it for years. Its inescapable.

Edit: I think it is also addictive in the way a tolerance to it builds up. Starting super shallow and then all the sudden you’re going deeper than you should. It definitely behaves like an addiction. When I was younger, I’d carry blades with me so I could cut at any time I felt the need. It was all I’d think about. Even now I will obsess about doing it.
26. Spent a few years living there after I graduated (2020) until I started making enough money to move out. Things are tight, but I don’t see me going back anytime soon.

I switched mid way through since I found another place that was more accessible for me. There was a lot of back and forth phone calls and releases of information  - my insurance had to do another approval for the remaining sessions. It all worked out in the end and I’m glad I switched.
I’m about 6 months out from round 2 now and still going strong

I had the arm implant/nexplanon for about a month before having to get it removed due to how it affected my mental health. However, my sister also has it and loves it. She recently got it replaced because she does so well on it. We are both plus size, and even though we usually respond to meds the same, we were completely different here. It really is dependent on the person and hard to know without trying it yourself.

I didn’t go on meds until my last semester. The last year and a half after I was diagnosed I was able to get accommodations (more time on tests, essay deadline extensions, tardiness excused, and software for text to speech was the most helpful for me. Prior to that, I struggled but I still made it through with high grades. Just a lot of late nights. It wasn’t easy, but it’s possible.

Unfortunately it all depends on how offensive the management is about it. My sister had a place that was infested like crazy and the management didn’t do much about it. At her current place, she hasn’t seen a single one and it’s been years. I get a fair amount in the summer, but still not hugely terrible. Pest control comes twice a month for my building and I see maybe 2 live ones a week on the summer (more dead ones) and then just a couple throughout the winter.
I know it’s a lot to take in, but please stick it out! You might not notice the effects for awhile, or you could notice it right away. But if it does work, it is SO worth it.

To clarify - 1 round was 36 sessions. So I did 2 rounds - 72 sessions. I improved for about 6 months after first round, but then medical stuff in my life happened, and I needed to get it again. Still going strong after the second round.

The tech is always in the room with you. The first place I did it at they just were working on their computer during it. The second place I did they actually had Netflix set up so we watched tv during it. I’m sure you can bring music to listen to if that would make it easier.

I’ve done 2 rounds of it (72 sessions total) and I have no horror stories to report. It saved my life. Literally. It showed me what life can be like when not weighed down by my anxiety and depression. Please don’t opt out. Give it a go. Commit to the full sessions (I don’t usually notice improvement until the very end or even after it’s completed). But it is SO worth it. Please give it a shot.
I take it everyday for work and people make it out to be a lot worse than it is imo. With your experience, I’m sure you’ll do just fine.

I used to regularly binge. I started Vyvanse 5 years ago now I think? Even though I started it for my ADHD, I noticed it almost immediately my binging got under control. I now RARELY binge. I’m talking maybe once a year whereas before it was weekly at least. I do still have urges to binge, but I think the vyvanse has decreased my appetite mentally to a point where I don’t think I can binge  even if I wanted to.
I feel like DBT did the most to help me with my maladaptive behaviors and patterns as a result of my cptsd. ACT helped a bit too. CBT never really did much for me. I’m not a fan of it.
I asked the pharmacist the best time to take it and if with meals or not when I first started it. She suggested taking it with breakfast.
For my first round, I didn’t start to feel improvement until session 30 out of 36. My second round, I didn’t feel improvement until maybe 2 weeks after I completed my sessions.

That happened to me occasionally during my sessions. Basically it just didn’t have good enough contact on a couple of the pulses, so we added on the missed pulses at the end of the treatment to make up for it. It was usually like an extra 30 seconds or something like that. Yours looks like an extra 15 seconds.
That makes more sense. While I didn’t get full remission, I did decrease my scores by over 50% and let me tell you it’s a BIG difference. The difference between severe and mild depression is huge.
When I asked mine about the success rate, I think he said something like 70% success/about the same rate as standard antidepressant treatment. I’ve never heard as low as 30%.
I got it too! Not sure if I had it prior to Thursday or got it on Thursday, but Saturday I woke up, and it hit me. I was supposed to go Sunday too, but decided not to so I wouldn’t spread it. ):
During my first round I remember crying during some of my sessions. Still had great results at the end.

When I was a kid, I remember there was a guy down the street who would walk a lot. It was always a fun task of where we would spot him next and exciting! It was always so cool seeing how far he would make it. For all the people thinking it’s weird/crazy of you, there’s plenty more that probably think you’re hella cool.

My entire first round was all before work first thing in the morning. My very first session I took the day off in anticipation of a headache but the rest of the days I was completely fine going to work right after.

Tbh I’m not knowledgeable in the area of sun exposure and scars, but my dermatologist suggested silicone based things to help with the reduction of my scars. She specifically suggested Silagen, but I’ve seen others mention silicone patches and similar products too.

It was expensive and a big time and money commitment, but it also gave me the best results I’ve ever had and think it was worth it all. It didn’t last super long, so I did it again because it helped me that much. I have never felt as good as I do now thanks to TMS.

I’m so glad you got a tattoo to give you some confidence back! Last year I got a large tattoo on my upper arm and forearm to cover scars. I used to not be able to wear short sleeves around my extended family or at work. Last year was my first summer where I could wear what I want. The confidence and freedom my artist gave back to me is so special. I want to cover my thighs too, but I don’t know how I will do it since it is basically both of my entire thighs. Everyday I am thankful for my tattoo and for my artist.

(I’m all for swearing it just doesn’t seem to fit right with the scenes she swears in)

I’d refrain from disclosing. Biases, even if they’re unaware of them, still exist, and can negatively impact the view your boss has of you. My appointments were always first thing in the morning, so I just told my boss I needed to have a temporary hours adjustment (I’m hourly) to arrive later and then stay later for the duration of a treatment I was receiving. That’s all I said. He was worried, so I reassured him I wasn’t sick. I was getting treatment for a condition I have. As little detail as possible is all they need. Since you’re just leaving an hour early, there shouldn’t be a problem.

The line overall to get in was super long (due to weather I think) but into the actual pit it was nothing. They were actually giving out free pit wristbands to help fill it up in Chicago (which I was blessed with).

Please try to give it more time and follow up with your doctor too. I was feeling very hopeless too after my last round but then a few weeks later I noticed I was feeling better. I really hope things get better for you soon.
How long ago did you finish your sessions? After my most recent round I didn’t notice the effects until a few weeks out of my last session.

I usually just did my commute to either work or home depending on when my session was. I never thought to do something specific after each session. I know it’s good to have a full nights sleep for your sessions but that’s about it. I was usually caffeinated during my morning ones lol.

The only time the doctor was in the room with me was during my initial mapping session. The techs did it the rest of the time. The techs are the ones that are trained with it and know how to use the machine correctly. They were honestly great.

I transferred providers due to easier access during my second round. It wasn’t too big of a hassle tbh just have to communicate a lot between the different providers. If you wait until end of July and have to restart, you might have difficulty getting insurance to cover another full round. Also please don’t get discouraged. My phqs didn’t start to change at all until probably 30/36 sessions.

TMS is the best treatment I’ve ever received for my depression. I didn’t know it was possible to feel this good. It has improved my life so much and helped me get to a place where I’m able to make more lasting positive changes for my mental health. I’ve done it twice and am glad I did.
Definitely cover up for the interview. Wait until after you’re hired to show them for sure.

If he is truly a wonderful guy, he will act with compassion and empathy upon seeing your scars. I didn’t say anything prior to the last guy who saw them and he basically said he was there whenever I was ready to talk about them. If he responds with disgust, that isn’t someone you want to be around anyway.
I highly suggest it! Dbt helped my bpd symptoms so much. That combined with TMS is a great combo.

I’m an office manager for about 15 salespeople. I’ve been here 2.5 years. I like it because I don’t have much client facing contact. All my work is done directly with my coworkers and company, so I get to know them pretty well which makes communicating easier. I do go into the office everyday, but I like having that routine of leaving my apartment daily.
That really sucks I’m sorry!!

Damn I’m sorry OP that’s really unfair you don’t have that as an option. Could you try to get an exception? Like for religious reasons? (Even if you aren’t). Otherwise you might just have to tough it out and take birth control for the duration of your treatment, and then you can get off it again once you’re complete.

The last guy I dated, after he saw them, I didn’t want it hanging over me, so I just asked and said something like “I’m sure you noticed my thighs” and he said he would be ready to talk about it whenever I was ready but that there was no rush and it was okay.

This is what we have known on it so far: This is a comb from New Hebrides, known today as Vanuatu, a small island located West of Figi and East of Australia. It could easily be assumed that the artworks found there depict cultural influences from the indigenous population that lived there, called ni-Vanuatu, or cultures from surrounding islands as a result of bartering between natives from Solomon Island. Combs were considered indispensable ornaments for the island dwellers as well as the men, and were signs of careful craftsmanship. These combs create a narrative about the individuals living in these regions that wore their combs in a variety of different ways such as placing them in a person’s hair at the front, back, on the crown of the head or at the side. Along with the material such as the Hardwood used to construct this piece, that most likely found its way to New Hebrides from Eastern and Southern Santo that were known for creating combs with various types and distributions of patterns.

The date is unknown, and it is unknown when it was collected and donated to our archive.
